items.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California
items.snippet: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).

items.title: The world mourns the passing of 'Star Trek's' Patrick Stewart with a galaxy of tearful tributes
items.snippet: "He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love."

items.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
items.snippet: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.

items.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
items.snippet: India launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite to orbit today (Oct. 30) atop a GSLV rocket. It was the fourth orbital launch from Indian soil so far this year.

items.title: 5 horror franchises that went to space... and one that absolutely should have but didn't
items.snippet: In space, no one can hear you scream, a bit like the empty theater screens that some horror franchise's final installments limp. But there are still some real gems among the space-based frightfests.

items.title: The rocket scientist who summoned demons: The true horror story of Jack Parsons
items.snippet: Rocketry pioneer Jack Parsons engaged in an elaborate series of occult ceremonies intended to summon an otherworldly feminine goddess into physical existence.

items.title: Neuroscientists reveal method to train people to have lucid dreams — and it involves virtual reality and meditation
items.snippet: People who had no recollection of a lucid dream over the past three years developed the skill after one month of performing a novel training regimen twice a week, neuroscientists report.

items.title: Spatial mapping reveals how human urogenital organs codevelop during organogenesis
items.snippet: A new study has mapped human urogenital development in its native spatial context, revealing how neighboring organs coordinate their development through cellular communication and molecular signaling during embryogenesis.

items.title: Scientists develop new system to boost prime editing in dicot plants
items.snippet: A new gene-editing system could make it easier for researchers to introduce precise genetic changes into crops such as tomatoes, soybeans and rapeseed. Developed by researchers in China, SmartPE improves prime editing efficiency in several dicot plants, addressing a major limitation of the technique.

items.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky—radio telescopes could help find 'ghost particles' origin
items.snippet: Neutrinos are funny little particles that weigh almost nothing, making them one of the universe's most elusive building blocks. They can come from objects as mundane as bananas and as exotic as supernovas—the exploding death throes of massive stars. Most neutrinos stream through space and pass through the Earth without interacting with anything.

items.title: Livestock guardian dogs enlisted in efforts to conserve Texas' smallest fox
items.snippet: In the Texas Panhandle, two livestock guardian dogs patrol a herd of cattle grazing the Rita Blanca National Grasslands. Although their singular focus is protecting the herd from would-be predators, their presence may make them wildlife conservation allies.

items.title: New home for orangutans rescued from Indonesia's burning forests
items.snippet: Deep in a forest in Indonesian Borneo, conservationists open a cage. A female orangutan and her baby waste little time, clambering up the towering trees and disappearing into the canopy, safe at last.

items.title: For many, striped bass fishing is a way of life. But the iconic species could face collapse
items.snippet: Striped bass fishing has been Bill Jakob's passion for more than 60 years, and he remembers an era when he'd spend all night casting his line into the crashing waves off Montauk and get eight or nine fish ranging up to 40 pounds (18 kilograms), a big catch by anyone's standards.

items.title: Chemists create disappearing tattoos: Here's the science behind how they work
items.snippet: How handy would it be if you could make your tattoos invisible for a job interview in the morning, and reveal them again for a party in the evening? This sounds like science fiction, but it may soon be reality.

items.title: Are narcissists multiplying or is the social media algorithm making them bolder? The answer in five stages
items.snippet: Social media doesn't necessarily reflect who you are, but it may intensify particular personality traits and confirm or even persuade you that your worst behavior is justified.

items.title: Hidden erosion: Study reveals soft mountain rock erodes three times faster than hard rock—with climate implications
items.snippet: A University of Massachusetts Amherst-led research team has discovered that weaker rock in mountain landscapes erodes three times faster than harder rock—even on gentler slopes—and is one of the main attributes governing mountain erosion. items.title: Tiny photonic chip links telescopes together to view the universe in 'astonishing' detail
items.snippet: A tiny glass chip developed by researchers at Heriot-Watt University has linked two telescopes together to enable them to act as a single powerful instrument, marking an important step toward a new generation of astronomical technology.

items.title: Crafted From Bone, This 2,800-Year-Old Flute Unearthed in Troy May Have Been Played Around the Time That Homer Composed 'The Iliad' and 'The Odyssey'
items.snippet: After more than 150 years of excavations, the object is the first musical instrument ever discovered in the ruins of the ancient city, which is located in modern-day Turkey

items.title: A Dog Left a Paw Print on This Mud Brick 4,000 Years Ago. Archaeologists Discovered It in the Rubble of a Bronze Age House
items.snippet: The brick was found at Tavsanli Hoyuk, an archaeological site in western Turkey. Humans and dogs in this region have had a close relationship for thousands of years

items.title: Madagascar's Giant Bats Seem to Be Shrinking. After Measuring 121 Specimens, Scientists Suggest Hunting by Humans Is to Blame
items.snippet: In a new study, researchers looked at museum specimens of the island’s flying foxes, spanning 150 years of history. They found a significant decline in size—right when commercial hunting ramped up

items.title: This Rosy Stone Spotted in the Sahara Turned Out to Be a 4.1-Billion-Year-Old Meteorite From Mars, One of the Oldest Ever Found
items.snippet: Martian samples this old are extremely rare and offer clues about the Red Planet's youth. This meteorite further hints that our celestial neighbor was once a watery world, suggesting it could've had the conditions to host life

items.title: Manga Are Black, White and Read All Over. Treasures of the Globally Popular Japanese Comic Book Medium Are on View in New York
items.snippet: The Brooklyn Museum's "Art of Manga" exhibition highlights the "mangaka," or creators, who have shaped the medium. Hundreds of original illustrations are making a rare trip to the United States

items.title: What Can Space Offer Humanity? In Pursuit of the Answer, Astronauts Have Been Making a Home in Microgravity for Decades
items.snippet: In a new gallery called "At Home in Space," the National Air and Space Museum shows how humans have tackled risky and arduous missions to push the boundaries of scientific discovery and exploration

items.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
items.snippet: A meteorite found in the Sahara is a rare piece of Mars' ancient crust.

items.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
items.snippet: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track.

items.title: UK could see 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
items.snippet: With high pressure developing across the UK, the start of November is looking very settled with no significant rain in the forecast.

items.title: To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan
items.snippet: Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure

items.title: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
items.snippet: The NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation; satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks
